new_visual_findings.observation: Source phase0 is upright and phase3 is already fallen. The generic median(0,3) normalization mixes standing and collapsed heights; use a reviewed upright reference for death, preserving every source pixel and death clock.
The declared front-left view repeatedly retains a front-right/right-facing skull and torso. Correct the whole view using a reviewed left-facing reference; do not mirror anatomy.
The initial upright hovering silhouette and later kneeling/collapsed phase3 are mixed as scale references. Use the reviewed initial upright scale, preserving the scythe/robe pixels and death timing.
All six declared back-left poses face upper/right, resembling NE. N and NE are already correct; replace only NW with a true back-left view.

The front-left strike stages face left, but the starting and restored guard turn front-right. Correct those mixed-facing guards while preserving the coherent leftward attack stages if a reviewed pose mix is feasible.
The loading pose turns the face and front torso right, between otherwise left-facing guard and strike poses. Keep a leftward-facing windup; the sword may wind back without reversing the fighter.
Standing phase0 and collapsed phase3 are mixed in the generic scale reference. Preserve the complete front collapse art; calibrate from the reviewed upright pose and retain the existing death clock.
The declared front-left idle retains the front-right canonical facing in all six poses. Other seven idle views are coherent.
Ready/restored guards face right around an otherwise leftward strike. Keep the front-left view coherent through all stages.
The ready/loading/recovery poses retain front-right facing while the thrust turns left. Replace this mixed-facing view using its correct W idle/run reference.

Full-resolution source inspection confirms an extra upright gem staff behind the extended horizontal staff in phase2. Phase3 has a single staff and an empty left hand, and can be reviewed as replacement contact via sequence [0,1,3,4,5].

Full-resolution source phase3 gives the staff to the left arm while the right hand opens. Other phases hold it in the right hand. Review [0,1,2,4,5] as a complete single-staff attack before considering new art.
The front-left hit sheet retains a front-right torso/guard. Backward head recoil in the other correctly facing views is natural and should be retained.
Upright phase0 and kneeling phase3 are mixed in generic normalization. Preserve the complete six-stage collapse; use the reviewed upright reference without changing source pixels or death timing.
The initial standing horse and collapsed phase3 are mixed in normalization. Use the reviewed upright reference to avoid enlarging the horse during death; retain all six original poses and timing.
The front-left idle remains front-right through the six poses. Its correct SW run can supply a same-character left-facing reference.
The declared front-left attack uses front-right ready/loading/restored guards around a leftward strike. Use its correct SW run as the camera reference.
Full-resolution inspection shows the six-pose front-left sheet retains the canonical front-right muzzle/torso; this is not merely a brief backward head recoil.
Check the generic upright/fallen median against the reviewed standing phase0. Change only materially affected normalization, preserving the entire wing/tail/sword artwork and death clock.
The front-left idle retains a right-facing human torso and spider body, duplicating front-right. Other seven main directions are coherent.
Front-right ready/restored guards interrupt the front-left claw strike and recovery. Correct the front-left guards; keep the valid leftward strike stages where feasible.
The initial brace/recoil poses retain a right-facing torso with the abdomen to the left, then recover to the correct left-facing body. Use the correct SW run as a camera reference.
Review upright phase0 against the current upright/fallen median and correct only materially changed scale. Preserve all six collapse poses, eight-leg silhouette, pixels and death timing.
The declared front-left idle retains the front-right muzzle/torso, duplicating SE. Keep the other seven idle views.
Full-resolution inspection confirms all six front-left run poses advance front-right. The pure W run is already left-facing and can supply a camera reference.
Front-right ready/loading/recovery poses interrupt the declared front-left axe strike. Rebuild only this mixed-facing view.
Full-resolution front-left hit source retains a front-right muzzle/torso through the brace and restored guard. Use a correct left-facing reference.
Standing phase0 and kneeling/fallen phase3 must not accidentally change body scale. Review the upright reference; preserve the complete axe/corpse artwork and death timing.

additional_detail.observation: Full-resolution phase3 puts the scythe in the left hand while the right hand opens; the other five phases preserve the right-hand grip. Review sequence [0,1,2,4,5] without changing original pixels.
